rv.q: It takes talent and chutzpah to somehow humanize characters that at first glance seem the very antithesis of human. Joy Gregory does just that in Saint Megan, the latest triumph from L.A.'s Rogue Machine Theatre.
Saint Megan is a brave, powerful and entertaining production. Rogue Machine has done it again, bringing us great theatre.
That and Patel's direction, which delivers spot-on performances from everyone — although it is Sorsa's unyielding matriarch that proves most fascinating and delivers the show's powerful catharsis.
The play is well written and skillfully directed, with an engaging cast that allows Rogue Machine another successful production – now selling out.
Clearly SAINT MEGAN is a thought-provoking piece which will remain with you well after the show is done.

cn.t: Gregory's compelling premiere finds humor and heart in a difficult subject, staged with skill and grace by director Patel and a strong ensemble in this excellent Rogue Machine production.
